Like the title says, lets chat about everyone's campaign settings!

I'll start:

My group is currently going from a premade setting (Forgotten realms; we started with the Lost Mines Premade), and are currently about to start in my new homebrew I'm making. Their characters in the FR were fighting a cleric and basically had their souls ripped out and tossed into a new plane of existance. Their new characters were the (un?)lucky people who just got an additional soul shoved into them.

The world they are now in was shattered in a giant magical cataclysm millenia ago, and the planet is held together as a much of floating continents (called shards) bound by magic. the ocean drained into the 'core' of the planet and springs up in certain continents. Water is moderately precious in some shards, and almost nonexistant on others. The shard the PC's start on is roughly based on pre-reconquista Spain, and should be pretty interesting.

What world are y'all playing in?
DM's and Players: Talk about your campaign setting!

My group is currently in the middle of a one-off adventure (which I'm now trying to figure out how to turn into a new world because they like it so much) in between the Lost Mines starter set as well. Long story short: we went on vacation together and they said they wanted to play so I concocted the (very unoriginal) idea of having them all fall into a magical dream world. I had them start off without telling them anything so they don't really know yet, but I'm placing clues every so often until they figure it out.

I spent a few hours with them asking questions and had them draw out the map together to enforce the idea that everything in the world is from their own heads (first clue about the dream). I'm also doing things like obscuring what time it is and the occasional deja vu, lots of fun :)

The part I'm most proud of is taking their existing characteristics to extreme proportions. So the bard, who is full of himself and thinks he is amazing, is known by every single person and thing in the world as the most amazing entertainer and they practically worship him. The fighter has an incredible imagination (always wanting to tear out spines and throw people off ledges in lieu of swinging a sword) so, unbeknownst to her, any feat of strength or dexterity will always succeed no matter what she roles. The wizard, who thinks she knows everything, has probably the most drastic effect: everything she thinks or believes to be true will instantly become true in the world. From the smallest thing to the biggest... she has yet to discover this yet thankfully so it isn't too hard to manage, but I'm really looking forward to this later down the road :)
That sounds pretty interesting. How many sessions are you in on thins new world?

Just two, we haven't played again since we got back. My problem now is that they don't want to go back and finish the starter set because it would be too boring, haha. I'll probably just keep playing in this world for awhile until it runs its course then go to my homebrew I've been working on :)

I've got a homebrew cyberpunk/sci-fi campaign going on. The party is becoming a sort of gang, and will be going toe to toe with the gangs and corporations that rule the cities. They can simply confront them in combat, or use the politics of the world to influence their control (I.E., planting a false set of plans from one gang to another, causing one alliance to break and another to form). Each city will have a different setup. They'll encounter a prison city, robot city, a kleptocracy, and even a colony on one of the moons.

I've taken inspiration from cyberpunk rpgs and made the system skill-based instead of role-based. They have 5 skills that level up, and having a level gives you extra abilities and better rolls (I.E. level 1 lets you add a d4 to your d20, up to level 6 where you roll 2d20). The idea is that once they've leveled enough, they'll be like the Matrix group, and their enemies will receive a similar boost.
